source.original_text: Faithful restatement of the fixed-point Gaussian calculation and Eq. (51). Fix one deterministic x of n-dimensional blocks and the deterministic source weights beta_i. Under the original unconditioned joint standard Gaussian of all ordered coefficients, let H_i(x) be the literal angular degree sum on the normalized x tail times the exact Eq. (16) cutoff, zero if a participating block is zero. The sum W=∑_i beta_i H_i(x) is centered Gaussian with variance V=n∑_i beta_i² C_i(x)² v_i, where v_i=∑_p a_i,p² with the exact Eq. (14) amplitudes. The source's expectation m(x) of exp(-W) is finite and equals exp(V/2). The source uses positive recursively determined weights and prescribed depth at sufficiently large n; the isolated finite identity extends to deterministic real weights and any positive n and natural depth. Only the coefficient law is integrated here, not the spatial law or an event restriction.

let g := fun (n : ℕ+) (h : ℕ) (i : Fin (h + 1))
    (p : {p : ℕ // Even p ∧ 4 ≤ p ∧ p ≤ 2 ^ (64 * (h + 1))})
    (u : Fin (h - i.val + 1) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n.val))
    (ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ
      ((Fin p.val × (Σ j : Fin (h - i.val + 1),
        Fin ((2 ^ (74 * (h + 1))) ^ j.val))) → Fin n.val)) ↦
  let S : ℕ := ∑ j : Fin (h - i.val + 1), (2 ^ (74 * (h + 1))) ^ j.val
  let a : ℝ := 1 / ((p.val : ℝ) ^ 4 * (S : ℝ) ^ 2 *
    Real.sqrt ((h - i.val + 1 : ℕ) * Real.log (2 * (2 : ℝ) ^ (64 * (h + 1)) * S)))
  Real.sqrt n.val * a * ∑ c, ξ c * ∏ s, u s.2.1 (c s)
;
∀ (n : ℕ+) (h : ℕ)
    (β : Fin (h + 1) → ℝ)
    (x : Fin (h + 1) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n.val)),
    let L := Fin (h + 1)
    let P := {p : Fin (2 ^ (64 * (h + 1)) + 1) // Even p.val ∧ 4 ≤ p.val}
    let B := L × P
    let C := fun b : B ↦
      ((Fin b.2.val.val × (Σ j : Fin (h - b.1.val + 1),
        Fin ((2 ^ (74 * (h + 1))) ^ j.val))) → Fin n.val)
    let E := fun b : B ↦ EuclideanSpace ℝ (C b)
    let degree := fun p : P ↦
      (⟨p.val.val, p.property.1, p.property.2, Nat.le_of_lt_succ p.val.isLt⟩ :
        {p : ℕ // Even p ∧ 4 ≤ p ∧ p ≤ 2 ^ (64 * (h + 1))})
    let S := fun i : L ↦ ∑ j : Fin (h - i.val + 1), (2 ^ (74 * (h + 1))) ^ j.val
    let a := fun (i : L) (p : P) ↦ 1 / ((p.val.val : ℝ) ^ 4 * (S i : ℝ) ^ 2 *
      Real.sqrt ((h - i.val + 1 : ℕ) * Real.log (2 * (2 : ℝ) ^ (64 * (h + 1)) * S i)))
    let χ := fun r : ℝ ↦
      expNegInvGlue (r - 13 / 20) /
        (expNegInvGlue (r - 13 / 20) + expNegInvGlue (7 / 10 - r)) *
      (expNegInvGlue (1 - r) /
        (expNegInvGlue (1 - r) + expNegInvGlue (r - 19 / 20)))
    let tail := fun (i : L) (j : Fin (h - i.val + 1)) ↦ x ⟨i.val + j.val, by omega⟩
    let c := fun i : L ↦ ∏ j, χ (‖tail i j‖ / Real.sqrt n.val)
    let field := fun (i : L) (z : (p : P) → E (i, p)) ↦
      if ∃ j, tail i j = 0 then 0 else
        c i * ∑ p : P, g n h i (degree p)
          (fun j ↦ NormedSpace.normalize (tail i j)) (z p)
    let Ω := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Σ b : B, C b)
    let H := fun (ξ : Ω) (i : L) ↦ field i
      (fun p ↦ WithLp.toLp 2 (fun k : C (i, p) ↦ ξ ⟨(i, p), k⟩))
    let μ := stdGaussian Ω
    let W := fun ξ : Ω ↦ ∑ i : L, β i * H ξ i
    let V := (n.val : ℝ) * ∑ i : L, β i ^ 2 * (c i) ^ 2 * ∑ p : P, (a i p) ^ 2
    HasLaw W (gaussianReal 0 V.toNNReal) μ ∧
      Integrable (fun ξ ↦ Real.exp (-W ξ)) μ ∧
      (∫ ξ, Real.exp (-W ξ) ∂μ) = Real.exp (V / 2)

blind_reconstruction.text:
Let n be a positive integer and h a nonnegative integer. Write [k] = {0,…,k−1}, L = [h+1], Q = 2^(64(h+1)), R = 2^(74(h+1)), and P = {p ∈ ℕ : p is even and 4 ≤ p ≤ Q}. Fix arbitrary deterministic real weights β_i and vectors x_i ∈ ℝ^[n] for i ∈ L, with the Euclidean norm on ℝ^[n].

For i ∈ L set m_i = h−i+1, J_i = [m_i], and S_i = ∑_{j∈J_i} R^j. For p ∈ P define
a_{i,p} = 1 / (p^4 S_i^2 √(m_i log(2 Q S_i))),
where log is the natural logarithm. Define the slot set D_{i,p} = [p] × {(j,t) : j ∈ J_i, t ∈ [R^j]}, the coordinate set C_{i,p} = {k : D_{i,p} → [n]}, and the real Euclidean coefficient block E_{i,p} = ℝ^{C_{i,p}}. The block labels are B = L × P. Let Ω = ℝ^{⨆_{(i,p)∈B} C_{i,p}} with its Euclidean norm, and let μ be the centered identity-covariance Gaussian probability measure on Ω. For ξ ∈ Ω, let ξ_{i,p} ∈ E_{i,p} be its coordinate restriction to block (i,p), with no rescaling.

For u = (u_j)_{j∈J_i} with u_j ∈ ℝ^[n] and z ∈ E_{i,p}, define the contraction
g_{i,p}(u,z) = √n a_{i,p} ∑_{k∈C_{i,p}} z(k) ∏_{(ℓ,j,t)∈D_{i,p}} u_j(k(ℓ,j,t)).
Let φ(t) = exp(−1/t) for t > 0 and φ(t) = 0 for t ≤ 0. For r ∈ ℝ set
χ(r) = [φ(r−13/20) / (φ(r−13/20)+φ(7/10−r))] · [φ(1−r) / (φ(1−r)+φ(r−19/20))].
Define the tail at level i by y_{i,j} = x_{i+j} for j ∈ J_i and the multiplier c_i = ∏_{j∈J_i} χ(‖y_{i,j}‖/√n). Define H_i(ξ) = 0 if any y_{i,j} is zero. Otherwise let u^{(i)}_j = y_{i,j}/‖y_{i,j}‖ and set H_i(ξ) = c_i ∑_{p∈P} g_{i,p}(u^{(i)},ξ_{i,p}).

Set W(ξ) = ∑_{i∈L} β_i H_i(ξ) and V = n ∑_{i∈L} β_i^2 c_i^2 (∑_{p∈P} a_{i,p}^2). Then V ≥ 0, W is μ-almost-everywhere measurable, and its pushforward W♯μ is the centered real Gaussian law of variance V (the point mass at zero when V = 0). The function ξ ↦ exp(−W(ξ)) is Bochner integrable under μ, and ∫_Ω exp(−W(ξ)) dμ(ξ) = exp(V/2).

import AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.SlcLsiQueryComplexity.RadialLevels

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open scoped BigOperators Classical
open AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.SlcLsiQueryComplexity.AngularDegree
open scoped NNReal

/-!
# Actual fixed-location weighted Gaussian and its exponential moment

Zhou–Suzuki, arXiv:2611.05813v1 (CC BY 4.0), the variance calculation
immediately before Eq. (51) and Eq. (51) itself. This integrates only the
coefficient sample, not the location. The source weights are deterministic;
arbitrary real weights give the same isolated finite-dimensional identity.
-/

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.SlcLsiQueryComplexity.WeightedRadialMGF

open RadialLevels

/-- The literal weighted field sum is centered Gaussian with the exact source
variance, and its negative exponential is integrable with the Eq. (51) mean. -/
theorem weightedRadialLevels_gaussian_mgf (n : ℕ+) (h : ℕ)
    (β : Fin (h + 1) → ℝ)
    (x : Fin (h + 1) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n.val)) :
    let L := Fin (h + 1)
    let P := {p : Fin (2 ^ (64 * (h + 1)) + 1) // Even p.val ∧ 4 ≤ p.val}
    let B := L × P
    let C := fun b : B ↦
      ((Fin b.2.val.val × (Σ j : Fin (h - b.1.val + 1),
        Fin ((2 ^ (74 * (h + 1))) ^ j.val))) → Fin n.val)
    let E := fun b : B ↦ EuclideanSpace ℝ (C b)
    let degree := fun p : P ↦
      (⟨p.val.val, p.property.1, p.property.2, Nat.le_of_lt_succ p.val.isLt⟩ :
        {p : ℕ // Even p ∧ 4 ≤ p ∧ p ≤ 2 ^ (64 * (h + 1))})
    let S := fun i : L ↦ ∑ j : Fin (h - i.val + 1), (2 ^ (74 * (h + 1))) ^ j.val
    let a := fun (i : L) (p : P) ↦ 1 / ((p.val.val : ℝ) ^ 4 * (S i : ℝ) ^ 2 *
      Real.sqrt ((h - i.val + 1 : ℕ) * Real.log (2 * (2 : ℝ) ^ (64 * (h + 1)) * S i)))
    let χ := fun r : ℝ ↦
      expNegInvGlue (r - 13 / 20) /
        (expNegInvGlue (r - 13 / 20) + expNegInvGlue (7 / 10 - r)) *
      (expNegInvGlue (1 - r) /
        (expNegInvGlue (1 - r) + expNegInvGlue (r - 19 / 20)))
    let tail := fun (i : L) (j : Fin (h - i.val + 1)) ↦ x ⟨i.val + j.val, by omega⟩
    let c := fun i : L ↦ ∏ j, χ (‖tail i j‖ / Real.sqrt n.val)
    let field := fun (i : L) (z : (p : P) → E (i, p)) ↦
      if ∃ j, tail i j = 0 then 0 else
        c i * ∑ p : P, angularDegreeComponent n h i (degree p)
          (fun j ↦ NormedSpace.normalize (tail i j)) (z p)
    let Ω := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Σ b : B, C b)
    let H := fun (ξ : Ω) (i : L) ↦ field i
      (fun p ↦ WithLp.toLp 2 (fun k : C (i, p) ↦ ξ ⟨(i, p), k⟩))
    let μ := stdGaussian Ω
    let W := fun ξ : Ω ↦ ∑ i : L, β i * H ξ i
    let V := (n.val : ℝ) * ∑ i : L, β i ^ 2 * (c i) ^ 2 * ∑ p : P, (a i p) ^ 2
    HasLaw W (gaussianReal 0 V.toNNReal) μ ∧
      Integrable (fun ξ ↦ Real.exp (-W ξ)) μ ∧
      (∫ ξ, Real.exp (-W ξ) ∂μ) = Real.exp (V / 2) := by
  intro L P B C E degree S a χ tail c field Ω H μ W V
  let v := fun i : L ↦ ∑ p : P, (a i p) ^ 2
  let σ := fun i : L ↦ (n.val : ℝ) * (c i) ^ 2 * v i
  let ν := fun i : L ↦ gaussianReal 0 (σ i).toNNReal
  let X := fun (i : L) (ξ : Ω) ↦ β i * H ξ i
  have hJoint : HasLaw H (Measure.pi ν) μ := radialLevels_hasLaw n h x
  have hMarginal (i : L) : HasLaw (fun ξ ↦ H ξ i) (ν i) μ := by
    have hEval := measurePreserving_eval (μ := ν) i
    have h := hEval.fun_comp_hasLaw hJoint
    exact h
  have hIndep : iIndepFun (fun i ξ ↦ H ξ i) μ :=
    (iIndepFun_iff_hasLaw_pi_pi hMarginal).2 hJoint
  have hXIndep : iIndepFun X μ :=
    hIndep.comp (fun i (z : ℝ) ↦ β i * z) (fun _ ↦ measurable_const.mul measurable_id)
  have hScale (i : L) :
      HasLaw (X i) (gaussianReal 0
        (NNReal.mk (β i ^ 2) (sq_nonneg (β i)) * (σ i).toNNReal)) μ := by
    simpa only [mul_zero] using gaussianReal_const_mul (hMarginal i) (β i)
  have hGauss (i : L) : HasGaussianLaw (X i) μ := (hScale i).hasGaussianLaw
  have hSum : HasGaussianLaw W μ := hXIndep.hasGaussianLaw_fun_sum hGauss
  have hMean : ∫ ξ, W ξ ∂μ = 0 := by
    change (∫ ξ, ∑ i : L, X i ξ ∂μ) = 0
    rw [integral_finsetSum _ (fun i _ ↦ (hGauss i).integrable)]
    simp only [fun i ↦ (hScale i).integral_eq, integral_id_gaussianReal, Finset.sum_const_zero]
  have hn : 0 ≤ (n.val : ℝ) := Nat.cast_nonneg _
  have hv (i : L) : 0 ≤ v i := Finset.sum_nonneg fun p _ ↦ sq_nonneg (a i p)
  have hσ (i : L) : 0 ≤ σ i := mul_nonneg (mul_nonneg hn (sq_nonneg (c i))) (hv i)
  have hVar : Var[W; μ] = V := by
    have hPointwise : W = ∑ i : L, X i := by
      funext ξ
      change (∑ i : L, X i ξ) = (∑ i : L, X i) ξ
      exact (Finset.sum_apply ξ Finset.univ X).symm
    change Var[W; μ] = (n.val : ℝ) * ∑ i : L, β i ^ 2 * (c i) ^ 2 * v i
    rw [hPointwise, IndepFun.variance_sum (X := X) (s := Finset.univ)
      (fun i _ ↦ (hGauss i).memLp_two)
      (fun i _ j _ hij ↦ hXIndep.indepFun hij), Finset.mul_sum]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ ↦ ?_
    rw [(hScale i).variance_eq, variance_id_gaussianReal, NNReal.coe_mul, NNReal.coe_mk,
      Real.coe_toNNReal _ (hσ i)]
    change β i ^ 2 * ((n.val : ℝ) * (c i) ^ 2 * v i) =
      (n.val : ℝ) * (β i ^ 2 * (c i) ^ 2 * v i)
    ring
  have hW : HasLaw W (gaussianReal 0 V.toNNReal) μ :=
    ⟨hSum.aemeasurable, by rw [hSum.map_eq_gaussianReal, hMean, hVar]⟩
  have hV : 0 ≤ V := mul_nonneg hn
    (Finset.sum_nonneg fun i _ ↦
      mul_nonneg (mul_nonneg (sq_nonneg (β i)) (sq_nonneg (c i))) (hv i))
  have hMGF : mgf W μ (-1) = Real.exp (V / 2) := by
    rw [mgf_gaussianReal hW.map_eq, Real.coe_toNNReal _ hV]
    congr 1
    ring
  have hInt : Integrable (fun ξ ↦ Real.exp (-W ξ)) μ := by
    have h := (mgf_pos_iff (μ := μ) (X := W) (t := -1)).1
      (hMGF.symm ▸ Real.exp_pos _)
    simpa only [neg_one_mul] using h
  exact ⟨hW, hInt, by simpa only [mgf, neg_one_mul] using hMGF⟩

end AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.SlcLsiQueryComplexity.WeightedRadialMGF

lesson.reader_note: The paper uses this quantity as a reference scale for the masses. At this point it is not an equality to the nonlinear gated weight at every sample. The later space integral and first-moment comparisons need separate arguments.

steps.title: Scale independent levels
steps.text: At a fixed location the actual radial levels have their joint product law. Deterministic multiplication preserves independence. Each scaled level remains centered Gaussian and its variance is multiplied by the square of its weight, even if that weight is zero.
steps.lean: Recover the component laws and iIndepFun from radialLevels_hasLaw, then use measurable scalar multiplication and gaussianReal_const_mul.

steps.title: Add means and variances
steps.text: Independent Gaussian variables have a Gaussian sum. Their finite first and second moments justify summing the means and variances. All mixed covariances vanish; the result is centered and its variance is the stated finite sum.
steps.lean: Mathlib's independent Gaussian finite-sum theorem supplies Gaussianity. The laws give the required moments. The proof computes the mean and variance and removes the nonnegative coercion using a sum of squares.

steps.title: Evaluate at minus one and verify finiteness
steps.text: A centered Gaussian with variance V has MGF exp(t²V/2); put t=−1. The formula also holds at V=0, when the random variable is zero almost surely. The strictly positive MGF verifies that the exponential is integrable in the formal real-integral convention.
steps.lean: mgf_gaussianReal uses the exact pushforward law. mgf_pos_iff gives integrability since the coefficient probability measure is nonzero, and neg_one_mul matches the exponent in Eq. (51).

lesson.lean_statement: HasLaw records the actual weighted pushforward, and Integrable is a separate conjunct before the displayed real-integral equality. The source constant is V/2, without a norm or factorization bound.
lesson.lean_proof: Product-law projections → deterministic Gaussian scaling → independent Gaussian sum with exact moments → the Gaussian MGF at −1. The source's degree-wise calculation is kept separate from the Lean reuse of the already verified grouped law.
